confidentiality clause = a term forbidding the sharing of the employer's private information
job-sharing = two people splitting the duties and hours of one full-time post
compressed hours = working a full week's hours in fewer, longer days
annualised hours = a contract that sets hours for the year, with busy and quiet periods
remote working = doing your job away from the employer's premises, usually from home
hybrid working = a mix of days in the workplace and days working remotely
hot-desking = sharing desks as they become free rather than having a personal one
outsourcing = paying another firm to do work previously done in-house
offshoring = moving work to another country, usually to reduce costs
minimum wage = the lowest hourly pay the law allows for most workers
living wage = an hourly rate set higher than the legal minimum, meant to cover basic costs
glass ceiling = an invisible barrier that stops certain groups reaching top posts
glass cliff = the pattern of appointing women to leadership only when an organisation is already in crisis
burnout = exhaustion and loss of motivation after prolonged workplace stress
work-life balance = a sustainable division of time and energy between job and private life
occupational hazard = a risk that comes with a particular job
severance pay = money paid to an employee when a job ends, especially in redundancy
statutory sick pay = the legal minimum an employer must pay when you are off work because of illness
maternity leave = time off work around the birth of a child for the mother
paternity leave = time off work for a father or partner around a child's birth
